correctness.rationale: The source update gives \(r_k=(I-\alpha_kA)r_{k-1}\). With \(\sigma(A)=\{\mu,1\}\) and \(\alpha_1=1\), one gets exactly \(r_1=(1-\mu)P_\mu r_0\). In the nonzero branch all later residuals remain in the \(\mu\)-eigenspace. The invariant bound \(q_k\in[0,1-\mu]\) implies \(1-\mu(1+q_k)\ge(1-\mu)^2>0\), so the norm ratio is exactly \(q_{k+1}=1-\mu-\mu q_k\). The fixed point and closed form follow by solving this affine recurrence. The endpoint minimax step follows by balancing \(|1-\alpha\mu|\) and \(|1-\alpha|\).

value.rationale: The class \(\sigma(A)=\{\mu,1\}\) is the canonical two-endpoint model underlying worst-case tuning of strongly convex gradient descent. The result reveals that exact endpoint annihilation, which can obstruct identification in other adaptive schemes, does not obstruct this residual-ratio feedback: after the top mode disappears, the remaining scalar trajectory still reconstructs \(2/(1+\mu)\). The exact alternating transient sharpens the source’s one-sided practical-estimator bounds and provides a concrete mechanism for observed parameter oscillations.
